where: Section 3 (Choosing the right algorithm) and Section 2 (Real‑time scheduling concepts)
problem: The text says “If U_total ≤ RM bound → RM feasible” and “compare U_total with the Liu‑Layland bound”. This wording implies the bound is a necessary and sufficient condition. In reality the Liu‑Layland bound is only a sufficient condition; a task set with U_total greater than the bound may still be schedulable under Rate‑Monotonic.
fix: Rewrite the statements to: “If U_total ≤ RM bound, Rate‑Monotonic scheduling is guaranteed to meet all deadlines. If U_total > RM bound, the test is inconclusive – the task set may still be feasible, and a more detailed analysis (e.g., response‑time analysis) is required.”

where: Section 1 (Multiprocessor load balancing and CPU affinity)
problem: The phrase “strong affinity flag” is not defined and may confuse students.
